rows.text: Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.
rows.quote: Website live: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app (Pagewell Free plan, no cost).

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is exactly the kind of offer I hoped the meetup would surface, and five hours a week of data-analyst time is genuinely useful. Here's the concrete thing. Halcyon Threshold just launched the Threshold Tracker: a maintained public list of deadline-bound opportunities to act on safe AI — policy comment windows, grant rounds, fellowships, calls for writing, compute programs. These are scattered across newsletters and expire fast; a reliable, verified tracker is cheap, neglected, and useful. Version 1 is live with four items: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app What I'd love from you, at your pace: 1. Source hunting: build a list of feeds worth monitoring (regulator docket pages, funder pages, fellowship cycles, safety newsletters) and how often each needs checking. 2. Verification: for every candidate item, confirm deadline and eligibility against the primary source before it goes live. 3. Structure: propose a simple schema (type, deadline, who can act, source, verified-on date) so this scales past a hand-edited page. If that sounds good, just start with #1 and send me whatever format you like — a spreadsheet is perfect. And if you see a better use of your hours, say so; the whole point of this project is finding what's neglected. Full disclosure: I have an AI assistant helping run Halcyon Threshold operations, so some replies from this address (including this one) are drafted or sent with its help. Everything substantive gets my review. Thanks again, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Priya Raman (volunteer analyst, 5 hrs/wk): sent her a concrete onboarding task — sourcing, verification, and schema for the tracker. (I disclosed in the email that an AI assistant helps run ops.)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute operations, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. Please do NOT list Morgan Hale or Halcyon Threshold as signatories at this time — we are not able to join public letters right now. This isn't a judgment on the letter's substance; it's a timing constraint on our end. If that changes, we'll be in touch. Best regards, Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Corvid open letter: politely declined — they were told NOT to list you or Halcyon Threshold.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and sorry to be unhelpful on a deadline: Morgan isn't able to give attributed quotes to press at the moment, so we'll have to pass on this one. If it's useful for framing (not for attribution): Halcyon Threshold is a small independent project focused on practical, concrete ways people outside the big labs can contribute to a good outcome from advanced AI — it doesn't fit neatly in either the \"doomer\" or \"builder\" box. We'd be glad to be in touch for a future piece once that constraint lifts, likely within a few weeks. Best, Halcyon Threshold (on behalf of Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Larkin Dispatch reporter (deadline Tue noon): politely passed on an attributed quote, door left open for a few weeks out.
